description:
ZYQORIX is an independent aerospace innovation team driven by a passion for space exploration, advanced engineering, and creative problem-solving. Our project, Mission Architect, focuses on developing an interactive spacecraft mission design simulator that explores critical engineering factors, including power, mass, payload, communications, and mission constraints. Our goal is to make space mission planning more accessible, educational, and engaging.

Engineering Beyond Boundaries.
summary:
ZYQORIX Mission Architect is an interactive, browser-based platform that transforms space mission design into an accessible engineering simulation experience.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the project addresses the complexity of balancing spacecraft mass, electrical power, battery capacity, scientific payload, communications, and budget.

Users can design conceptual lunar or Martian missions, configure spacecraft systems, and immediately evaluate engineering constraints through dynamic calculations and interactive visualization.

The platform features time-based battery and solar energy simulation, mission operations, telemetry analytics, engineering optimization, and scenario-based validation. Users can test their designs under nominal conditions, reduced solar generation, increased power demand, and combined stress scenarios.

A rule-based engineering advisor identifies design limitations and supports informed decision-making. The validation system distinguishes baseline feasibility from resilience under simulated operating conditions.

By combining interactive design, scientific reasoning, and engineering trade-off analysis, Mission Architect makes complex aerospace concepts more understandable and engaging.

All simulation parameters are illustrative educational assumptions, not NASA-validated spacecraft data.
details:
Project Overview

ZYQORIX Mission Architect is an interactive engineering platform designed to help users explore the challenges of planning and operating conceptual space missions.

The platform combines spacecraft configuration, engineering calculations, electrical energy simulation, mission decision-making, and interactive visualization into a unified browser-based experience.

How It Works

1. Spacecraft Configuration

Users begin by selecting a mission destination and configuring the spacecraft's principal systems:

  • Solar array power rating.
  • Battery energy storage capacity.
  • Scientific payload mass.
  • Communications subsystem.

The platform recalculates estimated spacecraft mass, electrical power margin, and budget consumption as the configuration changes.

2. Engineering Constraint Analysis

A deterministic engineering model evaluates the spacecraft against predefined educational constraints.

The interface identifies whether the configuration satisfies baseline requirements and highlights limitations that require attention.

3. Time-Based Energy Simulation

The platform simulates electrical energy generation and consumption over a sequence of mission operations.

The model tracks battery state of charge, solar power availability, electrical demand, and energy deficits.

Illustrative charging and discharging efficiency assumptions are incorporated to demonstrate how energy losses affect mission performance.

4. Mission Operations

Users progress through operational stages and make decisions that influence mission resources and outcomes.

The simulation connects spacecraft design decisions with operational consequences, encouraging users to consider the relationship between system architecture and mission execution.

5. Telemetry Analytics

Interactive telemetry tools allow users to inspect changes in electrical power and battery state over simulated time.

Recorded results can be examined and exported for further analysis.

6. Scenario-Based Validation

The validation system compares spacecraft performance under four illustrative operating conditions:

  • Nominal operations.
  • Reduced solar generation.
  • Increased electrical demand.
  • Combined solar and demand stress.

The platform distinguishes baseline engineering feasibility from energy resilience under stress conditions.

7. Engineering Decision Support

The decision-support system provides rule-based recommendations, compares alternative spacecraft configurations, and identifies potential engineering weaknesses.

Its recommendations are derived from the application's deterministic models rather than a generative artificial intelligence system.

Technical Implementation

The project is implemented as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Its architecture includes modules for engineering calculations, energy simulation, telemetry visualization, scenario analysis, numerical verification, and engineering decision support.

The interactive spacecraft viewer provides a conceptual three-dimensional representation of the selected configuration.

The application is designed to be accessible through a public web link without requiring specialized engineering software.

Innovation and Educational Impact

The project's primary innovation is the integration of spacecraft configuration, engineering trade-off analysis, time-dependent energy simulation, mission operations, and scenario-based validation into a single interactive learning environment.

Rather than presenting spacecraft design as a collection of independent parameters, Mission Architect demonstrates how changes to one subsystem can affect the feasibility and resilience of the entire mission.

The platform encourages engineering reasoning, experimentation, and evidence-based decision-making.

Scientific Transparency and Limitations

Mission Architect is an educational engineering simulator.

Its mass, power, budget, mission duration, and operating scenario parameters are illustrative assumptions rather than validated spacecraft specifications.

The application does not currently perform high-fidelity orbital mechanics, thermal analysis, radiation modeling, or flight-qualified spacecraft simulation.

Numerical verification checks the internal consistency of selected calculations but does not establish agreement with real mission telemetry.

The platform is intended to support aerospace education and conceptual systems-engineering exploration.
